_comment: Forge3D Timeline IR v1 -- PURPOSE SCHEMA for the tests/ir contract-test validator (validate_ir.js). This is NOT a full JSON-Schema document and does not claim to be one: it is a small machine-readable distillation of docs/TIMELINE-FORMAT.md (the normative spec, ADR-5) in exactly the shape validate_ir.js consumes -- required keys, primitive type names, per-kind record fields, enum sets and cross-field constraint names. Type names are the validator's own vocabulary: string, int (JSON integer), number, bool, array, object, vec3 (array of 3 numbers), color3 (array of 3 ints in 0..255), slug (^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$). Cross-field rules that a per-record schema cannot express (key order, array ordering, scene partition, fps reduction, raw-byte float hygiene) are listed under 'cross_field_rules' and implemented in validate_ir.js. If this file and docs/TIMELINE-FORMAT.md disagree, the spec wins and this file is the bug.
cross_field_rules: alphabetical key order at every object level (emitter guarantee 1)
tracks sorted by (scene, kind, character/target, start_frame); a keyed track's start is its first key's frame
keys within a track sorted by frame
scene spans partition [0, duration_frames) without overlap
raw bytes: no '-0' number tokens; no whole-valued float written with a decimal point (e.g. '60.0'); no BOM
all *_frame values, key frames and duration_frames are JSON integers
unknown keys at any level are tolerated (forward compatibility), never a failure

ease.note: One canonical spelling per curve; source aliases (slowly, gently, ease-in, ease-in-out, ...) are normalised by the compiler before emission and never appear in the IR. bezier arguments are Float-formatting numbers, comma-separated, no spaces.

constraints: text non-empty (byte-verbatim; an empty cue is a compile error, never a file)
scene is a SceneSpan id, speaker is a Character id
kind is one of enums.marker_kinds in files the v1 emitter writes; other string values are safely-skippable for readers (spec: Marker) and are NOT a validator failure

duration_frames >= 0 (the spec states end_frame > start_frame for records carrying end_frame; SceneSpan carries duration_frames and its partition rule is the binding constraint -- zero-duration spans from cue-less scenes are a known emitter/spec tension, see the Wave 2 B2 report)
spans partition [0, top-level duration_frames): first start_frame == 0, contiguous, non-overlapping, durations sum to duration_frames
keys required when resolved is true or absent; keys MUST be absent when resolved is false
key_constraints: each key carries at least one of value / value_deg (a number)
keys sorted by frame; no two keys with the same (frame, channel)

constraints: at most one camera track per scene
keys sorted by frame; no two keys at the same frame
exactly one of character (Character id) / target (scene object name)
keys sorted by frame; no two keys at the same frame
